PullRequest.Title: Fix HydraFusion visibility when signed out of GitHub
PullRequest.Body: This pull request fixes #342040 by ensuring that HydraFusion does not appear in the Agents window model picker when the user is signed out of GitHub.

Scenarios.Scenario: Signed-out Agents model picker receives BYOK bridge, root-configuration, or local-model-row updates
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The event synchronously reads the BYOK registry cache or local provider rows, rebuilds the in-memory model array, publishes it, and refreshes live session configuration. The new token check is on this local publication path and skips construction of at most the two fixed HydraFusion rows; it does not block on external work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronize available BYOK/local model rows into each live Copilot SDK session after bridge or local-row changes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one call per live session for a model-change event; model enumeration itself is one cached registry read for the serving window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-session synchronization occurred after publication before the PR; the added signed-in predicate neither adds calls nor changes session count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Publication to the picker completes before these fire-and-forget session synchronization calls; they are off the picker publication critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: O(B + C + L + S) existing publication work for B BYOK models, C cached CAPI models, L local rows, and S live sessions. The changed work is O(1): one credential-field read and a condition in a fixed two-entry HydraFusion loop.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Publication is synchronous per event. Existing follow-up model synchronization is launched once per live session without a shared limiter; this fan-out and its cardinality are unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: BYOK enumeration uses the bridge registry's cached serving-window snapshot. Signed-out model refresh already clears the CAPI cache and returns without starting the runtime or fetching models. The diff does not change cache keys, invalidation, retries, or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed line is inside a fixed-size local loop, and all publication callers and follow-up session synchronization paths were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneously live sessions and frequency of renderer model events vary, but those scaling mechanisms are pre-existing and unaffected. The changed constant work is bounded regardless of those values.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. While signed out, the PR reduces allocation and downstream catalog size by omitting up to two unavailable synthetic rows and introduces no boundary call or repeated work.

Scenarios.Scenario: GitHub sign-in or sign-out refreshes the Copilot model catalog
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Authentication is serialized, updates existing live sessions as needed, resolves account metadata, and schedules one coalesced catalog refresh. A signed-in refresh performs model-list and managed-settings runtime RPCs before calling _publishModels; a signed-out refresh clears cached CAPI state and publishes locally without those RPCs. The new check runs only at the final publication step.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update GitHub credentials in each live static-token Copilot SDK session
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one RPC per live static-token session per changed credential, executed sequentially; provider-backed sessions are skipped.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical sequential per-session credential updates occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These calls must finish before authentication proceeds to account resolution and model refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve Copilot SKU and, when a local-model provider exists, GitHub login/account metadata
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One SKU resolution per supplied changed token and at most one login resolution when a local provider is active.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These account requests were already on the token-update path and are not influenced by model publication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Authentication awaits these operations before scheduling the catalog refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stop/restart the Copilot client when credential mode, enterprise authentication, or a failed live credential update requires it
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one coalesced restart for accumulated reasons once chats are idle; ordinary compatible token updates need no restart.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Restart gating, coalescing, and chat-idle deferral are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A required restart precedes replacement catalog enumeration; busy-chat deferral keeps it off active-turn critical paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List models from the Copilot runtime
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One runtime RPC per effective signed-in catalog refresh after scheduler/in-flight coalescing; zero while signed out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single coalesced models.list RPC ran before publication; the new predicate is evaluated afterward.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The signed-in picker catalog waits for this result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve managed model settings through the Copilot runtime
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One runtime RPC per successful signed-in model-list refresh, with a timeout; zero while signed out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same policy RPC and ordering existed before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Publication waits for policy resolution after model listing.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing credential-update cost scales with S live static-token sessions; catalog transformation scales with C returned models. The diff adds constant work and can remove two rows from the signed-out output.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The authentication sequencer serializes credential transitions. Static-token live-session credential updates run sequentially. Model refresh scheduling coalesces repeated lifecycle triggers into one deferred refresh, and refreshModels joins an in-flight refresh; model-list and managed-settings RPCs execute sequentially.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Catalog refreshes are generation-guarded and coalesced; failures retain the last known CAPI list and retries use existing backoff. Sign-out clears CAPI models and avoids runtime enumeration. The added token read uses current in-memory credentials and changes no cache lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: authentication, restart, scheduler, model-list, managed-settings, and publication call paths were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote and runtime latency vary, but no changed line adds, advances, duplicates, or parallelizes those calls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR changes only final in-memory filtering and does not alter the expensive authentication or catalog-refresh boundaries.

Scenarios.Scenario: Signed-in catalog publication after periodic refresh or cached model-source updates
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A periodic refresh joins or starts the existing coalesced runtime catalog request, then transforms cached models and publishes them to the observable and live sessions. Cached BYOK/local updates can also republish without catalog network work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Runtime model listing and managed-settings resolution for periodic signed-in CAPI refresh
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One models.list RPC plus one managed-settings RPC per effective refresh after coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same calls and sequential ordering existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both complete before the updated signed-in catalog is published.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Publication remains O(C + B + L + S) in catalog entries and live sessions. HydraFusion candidate count is fixed at two, and signed-in behavior performs the same model creation as before plus a single precomputed boolean check.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Only one scheduled or in-flight CAPI refresh is effective at a time. Publication remains synchronous; existing per-live-session refreshModelConfiguration fan-out is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm BYOK/local publications use cached source data. CAPI refresh calls are coalesced, stale generations are discarded, and last-known successful models survive failures. The predicate does not affect any of these states.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: every _publishModels caller and its boundary placement was inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalog and session sizes vary, but the diff does not change their effective cardinality or any operation tied to them.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new signed-in condition is constant-time and neither increases publication frequency nor changes fan-out.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review of both changed files and all production publication/authentication callers. The only production change is an in-memory credential boolean used in a fixed two-model loop; it suppresses unavailable rows while signed out and introduces no additional I/O, IPC, subprocess work, unbounded retention, concurrency burst, cache change, or scaling cost.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
